reasoning: S1 is valid, but neither S2 nor S3 follows. Positive improvements can shrink to zero, allowing infinitely many steps within a bounded interval. In particular, convergence to beta does not imply finite attainment. Moreover, without regularity of nu, even the assertion that the limiting infimum equals beta is false.

issue.explanation: A decreasing bounded sequence need not attain its infimum. Boundedness does not preclude infinitely many strictly positive improvements whose sum is finite.

witness: For any beta<gamma_0<=1, define nu(gamma)=(gamma-beta)/2 on (beta,1]. This satisfies 0<nu(gamma)<=gamma-beta, and induction gives gamma_n=beta+(gamma_0-beta)2^(-n)>beta for every finite n. Thus the target fails even though the infimum is beta. Independently, S2 fails with beta=0, gamma_0=1, and nu(gamma)=(gamma-1/2)/2 for gamma>1/2, while nu(gamma)=gamma/2 for 0<gamma<=1/2. All stated bounds hold, but gamma_n=1/2+2^(-n-1), whose infimum is 1/2>beta.
